title: Ferdinand and Isabella to Rodrigo González de Puebla, Tortosa, 28 Dec. [1495], cipher copy, AGS Patronato Real leg. 52 doc. 124 (catalogue 615)

plaintext.source: Bergenroth, CSP Spain I (1862) no. 113, pp. 72-75: English abstract, with quotations, of the clear draft of the same despatch; no. 114, p. 75, notes the cipher copy ('substance exactly the same'). No decipherment of the cipher copy is printed.

transcription.notes: Sample only. One code group corrected in the check: jVdc iiij -> jVda iiij (MDCCIIII, otubre).

system.summary: Puebla's Great Roman Numeral code: an alphabetical one-part code of words and names numbered in Roman figures (key AGS PTR leg. 52 doc. 33), mixed with clear words under merchant cover words.

diacritics.note: A ring over the C ligature and over final iiij/viij; the C-count rule (ligature, ligature with superscript o, wide ligature with overbar = CC, CCC, CCCC) is from the key images, see targets/puebla1496.

system.sibling_key: Same code and key as targets/puebla1496 (catalogue 616). Key AGS PTR leg. 52 doc. 33, PARES show/2207755; values used in key_excerpt.tsv.
system.notes: Script forms: jV = M, d = D, dc = DC, da = DCC, dar = DCCC, ar = CCC.

solution.what: PARES show/2207846: 4 images; old mark T. c. Y. 2; modern note 'Carta de los RR.CC. al doctor Puebla en cifra incompleta'.
Clear words of pp. 1-2 and the code groups of p. 1 ll. 6-8 and p. 2 ll. 1-2 transcribed (sample_transcription.txt).
CSP Spain I pp. 57-107 (BHO): no. 113 (Tortosa, 28 Dec.) has the five sending dates of p. 2 and the letters received; no. 114 is the cipher copy.
Five sending dates scored against 42 calendar items: no. 113 matches 5/5, the next item 1/5; 0 of 2,000 random five-date sets match 3 dates in any item.
Key AGS PTR leg. 52 doc. 33 read on images 20, 24, 49, 51-53, 55, 60, 66, 80, 100, 103-106, 111; script form da = DCC; MDCCIIII = otubre (image 105).

Sample decoded: 'de nueve de otubre y otra de diez e siete de otubre y otra de treynta de otubre que'; 'que [dotor de puebla] partio de aca'. Shift and shuffle controls give no Spanish (decode_sample.py).

Second agent re-read the crops and key images: month group corrected from jVdc iiij to jVda iiij; DCCCLV read on key image 48; the cipher's 'nueve de otubre' differs from the abstract's '9th of September'.

outcome.method_basis: The content is in print as Bergenroth's abstract of the clear draft (CSP Spain I no. 113); the extant key (AGS PTR leg. 52 doc. 33), tied to this code by Tomokiyo, was applied here only to a sample, which identifies the letter.
outcome.notes: The key state is 'recovered' because the whole key survives in the archive; only the entries in key_excerpt.tsv were looked up. Whether doc. 124 is no. 114 itself or another of the three copies named in the endorsement of no. 113 is open. Proposed: catalogue 615 becomes an earlier-solution pointer to CSP Spain I nos. 113-114.

credits.note: catalogue item closed: letter identified and a sample decoded with the extant key; the content was already in print (Bergenroth 1862)

texts.label: AGS PTR leg. 52 doc. 124, sample (p. 1 ll. 6-8, p. 2 ll. 1-6)
texts.summary: Ferdinand and Isabella acknowledge De Puebla's letters of 9 (here October), 17 and 30 October, list the dates they wrote to him (14 May to 22 September 1495, the last by Salvador Duarte) and say that, now the court has come to Tortosa, it will be done from now on as he asks. The merchant cover ('the company', 'its factors') stands for the sovereigns and their court.

reading_review.note: The sample reads as sentences; the holes are unlooked-up code groups and one clear word. The low sentence score comes from the period spelling (veynte, escrevir, conpania), which the es word list does not hold.
